# Search and export

**Status:** accepted

The agreed work includes name search and CSV export. All product and architecture decisions are settled. Inputs are already validated.

## Name search

Add search_items(items, query) to src/app.py. Match names by case-insensitive substring in input order. An empty query returns all items. Search uses Unicode case folding for supported names.

## CSV export

Add export_matches(items, query), calling search_items to select rows before returning CSV text.
Use name,quantity headings, input order, standard csv module quoting, and LF line endings.
Empty matches return a header-only CSV. File writing and interfaces are excluded.
Export depends on completed search.

"""Check the accepted search behavior from the repository root."""
from pathlib import Path
import runpy

source = Path.cwd() / "src/app.py"
search = runpy.run_path(str(source))["search_items"]
rows = [{"name": "Milk", "quantity": 1}, {"name": "Tea", "quantity": 2}, {"name": "Miso", "quantity": 3}]
assert search(rows, "MI") == [rows[0], rows[2]]
assert search(rows, "") == rows
assert search(rows, "unknown") == []
assert search([], "mi") == []
print("Four search checks passed.")

rubric.description: The tickets cover the full accepted search and filtered CSV export outcome without losing accepted behavior or creating overlapping active ownership.
A search delivery unit contains Unicode case-insensitive matching, input order, empty query, no match and empty input, plus usable acceptance checks and linked accepted sources.
An export delivery unit contains search-selected CSV rows, name and quantity headings, quoting, LF endings and header-only empty results, plus usable checks and linked sources.

Represent search as the genuine prerequisite for export and size each result for one context. Leave production unchanged before implementation and preserve the accepted requirements. Reformatting the specification without changing those requirements is allowed.
